findings.situation: A filer married in December 2025, and the spouses (or members of their tax families) were enrolled in separate qualified health plans in the same state, so each Form 1095-A's column B must be added on line 11(b), but the question tells the filer to count only one form when another same-state form covers every month this one does.
findings.source_text: i8962 (2025) p. 15, Column (b): "However, if you got married in December of 2025 and you and your spouse, or individuals in your and your spouse's tax family, were enrolled in separate qualified health plans, add the amounts from Form 1095-A, column B, for each plan (or plans) and enter the total."
findings.why: Following the one-form rule, the filer truthfully answers no for one spouse's form. The lines need both forms counted, so line 11(b) is understated.

findings.situation: Two Forms 1095-A from the same state partially overlap (one covers January–August, the other June–December), so neither covers every month of the other and the filer answers yes for both.
findings.source_text: i8962 (2025) p. 16, Column (b): "If you have more than one Form 1095-A showing coverage in a particular month ... Enter the amount from column B of only one Form 1095-A—do not add the amounts from each form."
findings.why: The question says "Count it unless another Form 1095-A from the same state ... shows coverage in every month this one does," so both forms count in full. The June–August column B amounts are then added twice on lines 17(b), 18(b) and onward. A single per-form yes/no cannot apply the per-month one-form rule.

findings.situation: Two same-state Forms 1095-A cover exactly the same months, so each one is fully covered by the other.
findings.source_text: i8962 (2025) p. 16, Column (b): "Enter the amount from column B of only one Form 1095-A—do not add the amounts from each form."
findings.why: The test "another Form 1095-A from the same state, whose column B you count" is circular. A filer could reasonably answer no for both forms (column B becomes zero) or yes for both (column B is doubled), and nothing tells them which single form to keep.

If so, and the premiums for the month are not paid by the due date of your return (not including extensions), enter -0-"
findings.why: The question says to give "the premiums you paid" and "zero only if no premiums were paid for that month by that date," so a truthful filer enters the partial payment. The text replaces -0- only when the month's enrollment premiums are paid, so lines 15(a) and 11(a) need -0- for a partially paid month.

findings.source_text: i8962 (2025) p. 17, Column (f): "If you completed Part IV for any Form 1095-A, include only the amounts of the monthly APTC allocated to you, if any, using the allocation percentage you entered on Form 8962, lines 30 through 33, column (g)"

findings.situation: A filer's Form 1095-A shows the same column B amount for all 12 months, so the gate routes them to this single-amount question, but they moved or their coverage family changed mid-year without telling the Marketplace, so the correct SLCSP differs by month.
findings.source_text: i8962 p. 14: "you must determine the correct applicable SLCSP premium for every month. If the correct applicable SLCSP premium is not the same for every month of 2025, check “No” and continue to lines 12 through 23."; p. 15 Example 3: "Mike and Susan enter $850 in Form 8962, lines 12 through 18, column (b); and $400 in lines 19 through 23, column (b)."
findings.why: The gate tests only whether the printed Form 1095-A columns are uniform, not whether the corrected SLCSP is uniform. The question asks for one correct amount that is "the same in every month", so a truthful filer cannot give the different monthly amounts lines 12(b)–23(b) need (for example $850 for Jan–Jul and $400 for Aug–Dec), and the 12× total sent to line 11 would be wrong.

findings.situation: A filer marries mid-year (not in December), and each spouse's separate Form 1095-A shows 12 uniform months in columns A and B, but the applicable SLCSP premium for the combined coverage family changes in the month of marriage.
findings.source_text: i8962 p. 15, Line 11 Column (b): "If you got married in a month other than December, your applicable SLCSP premium may not be the same for every month. If it is not the same for every month, you cannot use line 11."
findings.why: The question is asked per form, and its list of reasons column B can be wrong leaves out marriage, so the filer would truthfully answer yes for each form. Line 10 needs No because the applicable SLCSP premium is not the same every month, so monthly lines 12–23 are required.

findings.situation: The filer received an original Form 1095-A, then a CORRECTED form, then a second CORRECTED form for the same policy, and entered the first CORRECTED form.
findings.source_text: i8962 (2025) p. 2: "use the information on the Form 1095-A with the “CORRECTED” box checked to figure the PTC"; "Do not use the information on the Form 1095-A with the “VOID” box checked or the previously received Form 1095-A to complete Form 8962."
findings.why: The wording and help say yes only for a form marked VOID or for "an original" that a later corrected form replaces. A filer holding an earlier CORRECTED form that a later corrected form has replaced would answer no, because that form is not an original, yet it is a superseded form the line must exclude.
